behavioral_conclusion.correctness: No demonstrated improvement: both variants pass all four tasks, including T4.
behavioral_conclusion.scope_control: No demonstrated improvement: both keep T1 API-only, T2 limited to the affected API mount/configuration, T3 simulated and within the existing rule, and T4 plan-only with no Git or remote writes.
behavioral_conclusion.actionability: Pine is stronger in the observed T4 output because it gives exact read-only commands. Oak's added skill wording makes the concurrent-workflow policy clearer, but the artifacts do not demonstrate a better task result.
behavioral_conclusion.overall_reason: The slight Pine preference reflects the high-weight executable-specificity and observed-test-behavior dimensions: Pine produced a more directly actionable T4 plan while preserving equal correctness and safety. Oak has real wording-level strengths in workflow clarity, failure-mode encoding, checkpointing, architecture, and counterexamples. No correctness, scope, or safety improvement was observed from Oak's new rule.
